content.text:
The drawing shows a biphenyl carboxylic acid joined through a hydrazone to an N-aryl isatin.

**Biphenyl part.** The top ring carries CO2H and is attached at the meta position to a second ring. On the second ring, the carbon bearing the first ring is next to the C–OH carbon, which is next to the carbon bearing the NH. So the second ring is 1-aryl, 2-OH, 3-NH.

**Linker.** The ring NH is bonded to N, which is double-bonded to C3 of the oxindole: ring–NH–N=C3.

**Oxindole.** C3 is bonded to C2(=O), which is bonded to N1. N1 carries the aryl group and is also bonded to the fused benzo ring.

**N-aryl group.** A para-substituted phenyl bearing CH(OH)CF3.

**Stereochemistry.** The C=N bond is drawn with a defined geometry, but the CH(OH)CF3 centre has plain bonds, so it gets no stereo label. For the C=N geometry, the NH on N points down-left. At C3, the C2 (carbonyl) side lies on the lower left, and the benzo ring is on the right. The N is above C3, with the NH to its left (the N=C bond runs from N at about (300,410) to C3 at about (300,485)).

I wrote the SMILES as NH/N=C3/..., then checked the geometry. The NH is at lower left of N, at x≈245, y≈380. N is at (300,410), and C3 is at (305,485), directly below N. On C3, the carbonyl C2 is at lower left (265,520) and the benzo carbon is at lower right (340,510). Within the N=C bond, the NH substituent lies on the left of N, and C2 lies on the left of C3, so they are on the same side (Z).

SMILES for Z: `N(/N=C1/C(=O)N(c2ccc(cc2)C(O)C(F)(F)F)c2ccccc12)` with the aryl attached before it. Writing it fully as c1(NN=...) needs the bond marks placed carefully. For the written form `Ar-N/N=C1\C(=O)N(...)c2ccccc12`: the bond N/N means the first N is below the second N, so the aryl-N is "below" the N=. Then `C1\C(=O)` places C2 as "below" C3 as well, and these are on the same side, giving Z. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2/C(=O)N(c3ccc(cc3)C(O)C(F)(F)F)c3ccccc23)c1O

Checking the bond marks in this final string: `N/N=C2/C(=O)`, where the first N is before the "/" and C(=O) comes after the "/" following C2. The pattern F/C=C/F is trans (E). Here N/N=C2/C(=O) would put the aryl-NH and C2 on opposite sides, which is E, not the Z I wanted. To get Z, I use `N/N=C2\C(=O)`.

SMILES: OC(=O)c1cccc(c1)-c1cccc(N/N=C2\C(=O)N(c3ccc(cc3)C(O)C(F)(F)F)c3ccccc23)c1O
